questions.prompt: Which sentence expresses a habit correctly?

options.text: My father is buying the newspaper every morning.
My father buys the newspaper every morning.
My father buy the newspaper every morning.
My father buying the newspaper every morning.

questions.explanation: "every morning" marks a habit, which takes the present simple, and "my father" is he, so the verb takes -s: my father buys. "is buying" is the present continuous, for an action happening now, not a habit; "buy" forgets the -s of he/she/it; "buying" alone has no am/is/are, so it is not a complete verb.

questions.prompt: Which time marker signals that the present continuous should be used?
questions.explanation: "At the moment" signals an action happening right now, which requires the present continuous (am/is/are + -ing). "every Monday", "usually" and "on Sunday mornings" all describe a habit, so they go with the present simple.

questions.prompt: Why is "I am knowing the answer" incorrect?

options.text: "Know" is a state, not an action.
"Am" is never used with an -ing verb.

questions.explanation: "Know" is a stative verb: it describes a state of the mind, not an action, so it stays in the present simple even now: I know the answer. "I" takes no -s and goes with "am", and "am" + -ing is perfectly correct with action verbs (I am reading), so the other reasons are false.

questions.prompt: What is the correct negative form of "She plays tennis" in the present simple?
questions.explanation: The present simple negative uses doesn't (does not) + the base verb for he/she/it. The main verb keeps its base form: doesn't play.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence correctly: "Look! Your brother ___ in the garden."
questions.explanation: "Look!" draws attention to an action happening right now, so we use the present continuous; "your brother" is he, so be is "is": is playing. "plays" and "play" are present simple (habits), and "are" goes only with a plural subject.
